scope: Unauthenticated calls to every /api/bugs verb and /api/login (direct :3002 and proxied :5173); forged and replayed localStorage sessions in headless Chromium; logout server-side effect; login error/timing oracle and 30-attempt brute-force check; stored XSS and SQL metacharacters in title, owner, description rendered on board, edit modal and delete confirm; CORS preflight from a foreign origin and text/plain simple POST; response headers; body-size limits (90 KB, 150 KB, 1.1 MB) and id edge cases; listener bind addresses; npm audit --omit=dev. Diff slice reviewed: users.json credential add, port 3000->3002 move, vite proxy, .gitignore, @playwright/test devDependency.
commands: curl -s -i -X POST localhost:3002/api/bugs -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"[security] unauth create","severity":"low","owner":"nobody","description":"created with no session"}'

curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' -X PUT localhost:5173/api/bugs/4 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"[security] unauth edited","severity":"high","owner":"nobody","description":"edited with no session","state":"closed"}'
for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST localhost:3002/api/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"username\":\"buggy\",\"password\":\"guess$i\"}"; done
git ls-files users.json; git diff users.json

findings.title: Every /api/bugs verb works with no session: anonymous read, create, edit and delete
findings.requirement: 03-login.md 'Only users listed in users.json are valid login credentials'; 05-logout.md 'prevent other users from using my credentials'; OWASP A01/A07, ASVS 4.1.1 (access control enforced server-side)
findings.evidence: No cookie or auth header sent. POST /api/bugs -> 201 (id 4); GET /api/bugs -> 200 full list; GET /api/bugs/4 -> 200; PUT /api/bugs/4 -> 200 with title/state changed; DELETE /api/bugs/4 -> 204, then GET -> 404. The backend listens on *:3002 (see security-07), so the same calls are reachable off-host. evidence/security/unauth-probe-1.txt, unauth-probe-2.txt
findings.fix: Have /api/login issue a server-side session (e.g. express-session HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie or signed token) and add a requireAuth middleware on every /api/bugs route that returns 401 without it.

findings.title: Session is a client-side localStorage flag; any string, including a non-existent user, opens the board
findings.requirement: 03-login.md 'Only users listed in users.json are valid login credentials'; ASVS 3.1/3.2 (server-generated session tokens)
findings.evidence: Fresh headless context with localStorage.buggyboard_user = {"username":"ghost-not-in-users-json"} and no login: /board loaded, URL stayed /board, 11 rows rendered, only GET /api/bugs requests made. The forged name also becomes the default owner in the New Bug modal (BoardPage defaultOwner). evidence/security/forged-session-board.png, browser-probe-output.json
findings.repro: In DevTools on http://localhost:5173: localStorage.setItem('buggyboard_user', JSON.stringify({username:'anyone'})); location='/board'
findings.fix: Derive authentication from the server session in security-01 (e.g. GET /api/me on load) instead of trusting localStorage.

findings.title: Logout is client-only: nothing is invalidated server-side and the stored value replays
findings.requirement: 05-logout.md 'close my session and prevent other users from using my credentials'; ASVS 3.3.1
findings.evidence: Logged in as buggy via UI: no cookies set, localStorage held {"username":"buggy"}. Clicking Logout sent no request other than GET /api/bugs; fetch('/api/bugs') after logout -> 200. Writing the captured value back into localStorage and loading /board restored the board. evidence/security/logout-replay-board.png, browser-probe-output.json
findings.repro: Log in, copy localStorage.buggyboard_user, log out, set it back, open /board.
findings.fix: Add POST /api/logout that destroys the server session from security-01; call it from logout().

findings.title: Diff adds a plaintext password (matt / <redacted>) to tracked users.json
findings.requirement: OWASP A02/A07, ASVS 2.4.1 (passwords stored with an approved one-way hash); 02-user-accounts.md requires users.json but not plaintext
findings.evidence: git ls-files users.json -> tracked; git diff users.json adds {"username":"matt","password":"<redacted>"}; POST /api/login with those credentials -> 200 {"username":"matt"}. Existing buggy/vanny passwords are also plaintext (baseline). Comparison is plain !== on the raw string. evidence/security/login-probe.txt
findings.fix: Drop the personal account from the commit (or rotate the password if it is real anywhere); store bcrypt/argon2 hashes in users.json and compare with the library's verify function.

findings.title: No rate limiting or lockout on POST /api/login
findings.evidence: 30 consecutive wrong passwords for buggy all returned 401 in ~1 ms each with no Retry-After/RateLimit headers; the 31st request with the correct password returned 200. evidence/security/ratelimit-headers.txt
findings.repro: for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST localhost:3002/api/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"buggy","password":"x"}'; done
findings.fix: Add express-rate-limit (e.g. 5 attempts/min per IP+username) on /api/login.

findings.title: Non-string login fields and malformed or oversized bodies return HTML stack traces with absolute paths
findings.requirement: OWASP A05, ASVS 7.4.1 (generic error messages); ASVS 5.1.3 (input validation)
findings.evidence: POST /api/login {"username":["buggy"],"password":"x"} and {"username":123,...} -> 500 text/html 'TypeError: username.trim is not a function at login (~/DEV/.../backend/src/authService.ts:19:36)'. Malformed JSON -> 400 SyntaxError trace; 150 KB body -> 413 PayloadTooLargeError trace. Server stayed healthy. Express only hides traces when NODE_ENV=production, which this dev run does not set. evidence/security/login-probe.txt, resource-probe.txt
findings.fix: Coerce with typeof x === 'string' ? x : '' in /api/login (as the bug routes do) and add a final error handler that returns JSON {error,message} without the stack.

findings.title: Backend listens on all interfaces (*:3002) while the UI binds to loopback only
findings.evidence: lsof: node 5305 TCP *:3002 (LISTEN); node 4244 TCP [::1]:5173 (LISTEN). app.listen(PORT) passes no host. Off-host reachability was not tested (localhost-only rule). Pre-existing: the diff changed only the port number. evidence/security/listeners.txt

findings.title: Missing security headers and X-Powered-By: Express on API responses
findings.requirement: OWASP A05, ASVS 14.4 (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy); ASVS 14.3.3
findings.evidence: API responses carry X-Powered-By: Express and no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or Referrer-Policy. The Vite dev document (/login) has none either, but that is dev-server behaviour and not representative of production. evidence/security/unauth-probe-1.txt, ratelimit-headers.txt

findings.title: Lax bug-id parsing: '1 OR 1=1', '1;DROP TABLE bugs', '1.9', '1e3' resolve to bug 1
findings.evidence: GET /api/bugs/1%20OR%201=1 and /api/bugs/1;DROP%20TABLE%20bugs -> 200 bug 1; 1.9 and 1e3 -> 200 (bug 1); ' 2' -> 200; 0x10 -> 404; abc -> 400. Not SQL injection (the id is bound), but PUT/DELETE parse ids the same way, so a malformed id acts on a real bug. DELETE with a malformed id was not run, so shared data stayed intact. evidence/security/injection-probe.txt
findings.fix: Reject ids that do not match /^[1-9]\d*$/ with 400.

findings.title: No per-field length limit: a 90 KB title is stored and rendered
findings.requirement: ASVS 5.1.4 (field length validation); bounded resource use
findings.evidence: POST with a 90,000-char title -> 201 (id 6, deleted afterwards). The express.json default 100 KB body limit held: 150 KB and 1.1 MB bodies -> 413. Anonymous callers can therefore add about 100 KB per request with no count limit. evidence/security/resource-probe.txt
findings.fix: Cap title/owner/description (e.g. 200/100/10000 chars) in createBug/updateBug and return 400.

findings.title: Specs contain no security requirements (API authentication, session, password storage, brute-force)
findings.requirement: Missing requirement: specs/features/02,03,05 describe only UI-level login/logout
findings.evidence: No clause requires the API to authenticate callers, sessions to be server-issued or invalidated, passwords to be hashed, or login attempts to be limited. The ASVS L1 baseline was applied in their place.
findings.fix: Add a security spec covering API auth on every /api/bugs route, server session lifecycle, hashed passwords and login throttling.

notTested: TLS, HSTS, cookie flags and production headers: local dev server over plain HTTP, no cookies issued, Vite dev document headers are not production headers
Off-host reachability of *:3002 (localhost-only rule); bind address shown by lsof only
Authorization / per-user ownership: deliberately unowned, no role model
Statistically meaningful timing oracle: only single-sample timings (~1.2 ms for unknown user and wrong password); plaintext compare means no hashing-cost difference
DELETE/PUT with malformed ids (not run, to avoid mutating other agents' bugs)
Sustained brute force or flood beyond 30 login attempts and single 1.1 MB bodies (shared server)
Frontend dev dependencies (npm audit run with --omit=dev as instructed)
Git history secret scan beyond users.json
